questions.q: Write the balanced chemical equation for the preparation of propan-2-ol from 2-bromopropane using aqueous NaOH. Identify the reaction mechanism (SN1 or SN2) and justify your choice based on the substrate structure.
questions.a: CH3CHBrCH3 + NaOH(aq) → CH3CH(OH)CH3 + NaBr. Mechanism: SN1 because 2-bromopropane is a secondary alkyl halide; the carbocation CH3C+HCH3 is relatively stable and the reaction proceeds via carbocation formation in polar protic solvent. A wrong answer (e.g., writing SN2 or using alcoholic KOH) reveals confusion between substitution/elimination conditions and carbocation stability trends.

questions.q: Explain why acid-catalyzed hydration of propene yields propan-2-ol as the major product, while hydroboration-oxidation of propene yields propan-1-ol as the major product. Use the terms "carbocation stability" and "anti-Markovnikov addition" in your answer.
questions.a: In acid-catalyzed hydration, H+ adds to the less substituted carbon of propene to form the more stable secondary carbocation (CH3C+HCH3), then water attacks giving propan-2-ol (Markovnikov). In hydroboration-oxidation, borane adds with boron attaching to the less hindered terminal carbon; oxidation replaces B with OH, yielding propan-1-ol (anti-Markovnikov). A wrong answer that swaps the products or omits carbocation stability shows misunderstanding of regioselectivity origins.

questions.q: Predict the major alcohol product when 3-methylbut-1-ene undergoes (a) acid-catalyzed hydration and (b) hydroboration-oxidation. Draw the structures and name them.
questions.a: (a) Acid-catalyzed hydration: H+ adds to C1 forming secondary carbocation at C2; a hydride shift from C3 yields a more stable tertiary carbocation at C3. Water attacks to give 3-methylbutan-2-ol (major) and some 2-methylbutan-2-ol after rearrangement. (b) Hydroboration-oxidation: boron adds to terminal carbon, oxidation gives 3-methylbutan-1-ol (anti-Markovnikov, no rearrangement). A wrong answer that ignores carbocation rearrangement in (a) or gives Markovnikov product for (b) reveals gaps in mechanism understanding.

questions.q: Compare the reaction conditions and stereochemical outcomes of acid-catalyzed hydration and hydroboration-oxidation for a chiral alkene like (Z)-but-2-ene. Which method gives a racemic mixture and why?
questions.a: Acid-catalyzed hydration proceeds via planar carbocation, so water attacks from both faces giving racemic butan-2-ol. Hydroboration-oxidation involves syn addition of H and OH across the double bond; for (Z)-but-2-ene, syn addition yields a meso compound (if applicable) or specific stereoisomers, but not a racemic mixture because the addition is stereospecific. A wrong answer claiming both give racemic mixtures misses the stereospecific syn addition of hydroboration.

questions.q: A student attempts to prepare tert-butanol from 2-methylpropene using concentrated H2SO4 followed by water. They observe a low yield of tert-butanol and formation of an alkene by-product. Evaluate the likely error and suggest the correct condition.
questions.a: Concentrated H2SO4 at high temperature causes elimination (dehydration) to reform the alkene or form di-tert-butyl ether. Correct condition: dilute H2SO4 (or H3PO4) at lower temperature (e.g., 353 K) to favor hydration over elimination. A wrong answer blaming the alkene structure instead of reaction conditions shows inability to distinguish substitution vs elimination competition.

questions.q: Design a two-step synthesis of 2-phenylethanol starting from styrene (phenylethene). Specify reagents for each step and explain why your chosen route avoids carbocation rearrangement.
questions.a: Step 1: Hydroboration-oxidation of styrene with (BH3)2 then H2O2/NaOH gives 2-phenylethanol directly (anti-Markovnikov, no carbocation). Alternative: acid-catalyzed hydration would give 1-phenylethanol via benzylic carbocation (Markovnikov). The designed route avoids rearrangement because hydroboration does not involve carbocation intermediates. A poor answer using acid hydration shows failure to apply regioselectivity control.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Alcohols can be prepared from haloalkanes via nucleophilic substitution (SN1/SN2) using aqueous NaOH/KOH, and from alkenes via ______ addition: acid-catalyzed hydration (Markovnikov) or hydroboration-oxidation (anti-Markovnikov).
Fill in the blank: Observe how adding water to an alkene in the presence of acid yields an alcohol — this is the ______ route to ethanol from ethene.
Fill in the blank: For anti-Markovnikov addition, hydroboration-oxidation uses borane to add BH______ to the less substituted carbon, then oxidation replaces B with OH.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can write balanced equations and stepwise mechanisms for both preparation routes, predict major products considering carbocation stability and regioselectivity, and choose appropriate reagents (aqueous NaOH for haloalkanes, dilute H2SO4 for Markovnikov hydration, (BH3)2 then H2O2/NaOH for anti-Markovnikov hydration).
